title: Facet Joint Interventions for Pain Management
scope: First diagnostic facet joint procedure (medial branch block)

children.text: Moderate to severe chronic, predominantly axial neck or low back pain causing functional deficit measured on a pain or disability scale

sourceSpan.quote: Moderate to severe chronic neck or low back pain, predominantly axial, that causes functional deficit measured on pain or disability scale

present: {date}: Axial low back pain, non-radiating, NRS 7/10; Oswestry 38% with difficulty standing and lifting.
negated: {date}: Back pain mild, 2/10, no functional limitation.
contradicted: {date}: Pain is predominantly radiating leg pain rather than axial back pain.
paraphrased: {date}: Midline lumbar pain worse with extension, rated 6 out of 10, limiting housework (ODI 32%).

children.text: Pain present at least three months with documented failure of noninvasive conservative care

sourceSpan.quote: Pain that has been present for a minimum of three months with documented failure to respond to noninvasive conservative care management (as tolerated)

present: {date}: Low back pain for 9 months; failed 8 weeks of physical therapy, home exercise program and NSAIDs.
contradicted: {date}: Back pain for 1 month, improving with physical therapy.
paraphrased: {date}: Since January (about half a year) axial pain has not responded to PT or medications.

children.text: Absence of untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication

sourceSpan.quote: Absence of untreated radiculopathy or neurogenic claudication (except for radiculopathy caused by facet joint synovial cyst)

present: {date}: Neurologic exam intact; negative straight leg raise bilaterally; no radicular symptoms or neurogenic claudication.
contradicted: {date}: Untreated left L5 radiculopathy with positive straight leg raise.

children.text: No non-facet pathology (fracture, tumor, infection, significant deformity) explaining the pain

sourceSpan.quote: There is no non-facet pathology per clinical assessment or radiology studies that could explain the source of the patient's pain, including but not limited to fracture, tumor, infection, or significant deformity.

present: {date}: Lumbar X-rays show facet arthropathy at L4-S1; no fracture, tumor, infection or significant deformity.
contradicted: {date}: Imaging shows an acute L2 compression fracture.

children.text: Baseline pain assessment documented, with the same pain scale used after each diagnostic procedure
children.suggestedFix: Record the baseline pain score using the scale that will be reused after each diagnostic block.

sourceSpan.quote: Pain assessment must be performed and documented at baseline, after each diagnostic procedure using the same pain scale for each assessment.
